content.title: About
content.content: Pea salad with cheese is a light dish that combines boiled green peas, soft cottage or melt cheese, fresh vegetables, and a light dressing. It is popular as an appetizer, side dish, or a light meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peas are one of the oldest legume crops, cultivated for over 7,000 years.
The cheese can be either fresh cottage cheese or aged cheese, changing the flavor and texture of the salad.
Pea salad is often served cold, but it can also be gently warmed.
In some regions, mint or dill is added for extra aroma.
The dish is easily adapted to a vegetarian diet by using a plant‑based cheese alternative.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Peas provide about 5 g of protein per 100 g, helping to maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Peas and cheese together supply B1, B6, and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Cheese adds a substantial amount of calcium and phosphorus, supporting bone health.

items.title: Low fat when using low‑fat cheese
items.content: Choosing cottage cheese or low‑fat melt cheese can keep the calorie count modest.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy should replace cheese with a plant‑based alternative.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some melt cheeses can be high in salt; opt for low‑sodium varieties.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Legumes, including peas, may cause bloating in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled, garnished with fresh herbs. It can be added to sandwiches, used as a filling for wraps, or enjoyed as a standalone snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, keep cheese separate from peas to prevent excess moisture.
